memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Three days after they made the treaty with the Gibeonites, the Israelites heard that they were neighbors, living near them. So the Israelites set out and on the third day came to their cities: Gibeon, Kephirah, Beeroth and Kiriath Jearim. But the Israelites did not attack them, because the leaders of the assembly had sworn an oath to them by the Lord, the God of Israel. The whole assembly grumbled against the leaders. — Josh 9:16-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Just three days later, the truth comes out. The "distant travellers" turn out to be near neighbours. The deception is exposed, and the people are furious. But notice what happens next: even though the treaty was made under false pretences, Israel does not attack the Gibeonites, "because the leaders... had sworn an oath to them by the Lord."

This is a striking and important moment. The treaty had been secured by deception. By any human reckoning, Israel would have been justified in tearing it up. Yet because they had made a solemn oath in God's name, they held to it. Their word, once given before God, was binding — even though they had been tricked into giving it.

Here is a searching lesson about the seriousness of our promises. Israel understood that an oath sworn in the name of the Lord could not be casually broken, whatever the circumstances. To break it would dishonour the God in whose name it was made. God's people are to be people of their word, even when keeping that word is costly and inconvenient.

We live in an age where promises are broken cheaply — commitments abandoned when they become difficult, agreements discarded when they no longer suit us. But God's people are called to a higher standard. The righteous person, the Psalmist says, is one "who keeps an oath even when it hurts, and does not change their mind" (Ps 15:4). Our God always keeps His word to us; He never breaks covenant. As His people, we are called to reflect His faithfulness by being people whose word can be trusted.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you a person whose word can be trusted, even when keeping it is costly?
2. Have you ever been tempted to break a commitment because it became inconvenient?
3. How does God's own unfailing faithfulness inspire you to keep your word?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You always keep Your word and never break covenant. Make me a person of integrity, who keeps my promises even when it hurts, reflecting Your faithfulness. Amen.
